title: The IaC trust model
breadcrumb: Wire up Deploy App TAK Servers via a Federation Hub (IaC)

headings.text: Give the hub an identity from Deploy App
Use a unique CA per deployment

blocks.html:
Federation uses mutual TLS, so a link works only if both ends trust each other's CA. With a handful of Deploy App deployments and one hub, that trust matrix is small and fully known, so you can set it up in code. You own every CA and you inject secrets at deploy time, so no manual uploads are needed.

The certificates involved

Each Deploy App deployment has its own PKI (RASENMAEHER plus CFSSL on the Legacy/Docker stack, or opendefence-pki on Kubernetes). At first run the TAK Server:

  • gets its server certificate from RASENMAEHER (…/product/sign_csr/mtls), and
  • builds its truststore from the CA PEMs in /ca_public/ (importing root_ca.pem, intermediate_ca.pem, and miniwerk_ca.pem if present, each by alias), then copies it to fed-truststore.jks, the federation truststore.

So a deployment's federation CA is its root_ca.pem (plus intermediate). That PEM is what another party must trust to accept this deployment.

Give the hub an identity from Deploy App

Treat the Federation Hub as a Deploy App product: enroll it and sign its server/client certs through RASENMAEHER (sign_csr). Its cert then chains to a CA you already manage, and you avoid running a separate, untracked CA. You can give the hub its own CA instead; if you do, that CA's PEM is the one you distribute below.

The trust matrix

each server CA  ─────────▶  hub fed-truststore     (so the hub accepts the servers)
   hub CA          ─────────▶  each server /ca_public  (so the servers accept the hub)

Two one-way injections, applied to every node by the pipeline:

  1. Server CA to the hub. For each deployment, take its root_ca.pem, put it in the hub's federation truststore, and register it as a CA Group in the policy (see Policy as code).
  2. Hub CA to the servers. Take the hub's CA PEM and drop it into each deployment's /ca_public/ with a unique filename (for example fedhub_ca.pem), so first run imports it into fed-truststore.jks.

The set of CAs is known to your IaC (it knows which deployments exist), so this is just collecting the CA PEMs and fanning them out to the right truststores.

Isolate federation trust

By default Deploy App copies the same truststore to both fed-truststore.jks and the client truststore-root.jks. If you inject a peer/hub CA into /ca_public/, it lands in both, which means a client holding a peer-CA cert could also connect directly on 8089. For cleaner isolation, build a dedicated fed-truststore.jks that contains only the federation CAs (your own plus the hub), separate from the client truststore. The TAK Server configuration guide recommends this separation.

Use a unique CA per deployment

Keep one CA per deployment, which you already do (each has its own RASENMAEHER/CFSSL). If two servers shared a CA, the hub could treat them as Interconnected and share everything between them automatically. Distinct CAs are what let the policy control each link on its own.
